cohort: The study included 2472 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies who delivered between December 1, 2022, and February 1, 2023.
finding: Acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at delivery was associated with higher risks of ICP, preterm birth, fetal distress, primary cesarean delivery, and neonatal unit admission, while prior SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy was linked to increased risk of ICP.
mod_finding: Acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at delivery was associated with a higher rate of primary cesarean delivery.
